content:
ana: Heads-up: noticed several customers reporting lower-quality outputs. Root cause looks like some v2 requests ended up on v1 during a quota enforcement window.
mike: Do we have an example log?
ana: Pasting sanitized edge log snippet:
```
[2025-04-13T01:42:12Z] req=R12 route=acct/beta variant=v2 status=THROTTLED fallback=acct/beta:v1 reason=RATE_CAP
[2025-04-13T01:42:12Z] routing_decision=sticky_match -> selected=acct/beta:v1
```
sarah: If sticky_match is beating explicit fallback when reason==RATE_CAP that's a bug in precedence. We should prefer configured fallback on capacity problems.
mike: Agreed. Two parts: (A) router precedence logic, (B) telemetry + console so tenants can see when fallback happens.
ana: Telemetry idea: emit `route.fallback` event with tags: route, tenant, from_variant, to_variant, reason. Keep tag values low-cardinality (reason ∈ {rate_cap, sticky, header}). Sample full traces 0.5% to keep costs down.
sarah: Console UX: add a per-route micro-metric row: "Fallbacks (last 1h)" and an incident banner when rate_cap fallbacks > threshold. Banner copy: "Some requests were served by fallback variant v1 due to capacity limits. Consider increasing reserved capacity or enabling a dedicated route."
mike: Implementation plan: 1) quick hotfix to router to make fallback win for RATE_CAP (feature-flagged) -> owner: mike, ETA: today EOD. 2) telemetry schema + metric registration -> owner: sarah, ETA: tomorrow. 3) console mock + banner copy -> owner: product (TBD), ETA: tomorrow AM. 4) ops saved search for support -> owner: ops, ETA: today.
sarah: Also, add a low-cardinality `fallback_reason` tag and a boolean `fallback_decision` in structured logs so infra can backfill for past hour.
mike: Will add unit tests: simulate throttle then sticky_match and assert fallback branch taken. Will ship behind `router.fallback_precedence_fix` flag.
ops-bot: Deploy queued: mike/router-fallback-prec -> canary in prod-1 at 2025-04-13T06:00:00Z.
nana: After canary, run shadow-ratecap on 1% traffic and verify `route.fallback` increments but no visible customer disruptions.
sarah: Also tie fallback metric to billing dashboard so customers can correlate throttles -> reduce noise by exposing aggregated counts and a link to sampled examples.
mike: One more note: we found a variant header normalization oddity in some gateways where `X-Client-Variant` was rewritten to lowercase and snake_case; adding audit logs for header normalization changes outcome might catch those.
sarah: Good call. Add `header_norm` as potential fallback reason and include short tooltip in console telling integrators to avoid mutating Redwood headers.
nana: Action items repeated in thread. Will track in a quick ticket. Thanks all.
